hypothesis: H31: actual OS subprocess timeout/nonzero-exit errors from an owned replacement extractor preserve the cached/fresh delivery distinction and durable bytes previously observed with synthetic exception injection.

owned_child_policy.environment: Explicit minimal PATH/PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE; no inherited private environment values
owned_child_policy.code: Only stdlib os/sys/json/time; emit own PID and requested mode, then deliberate bounded wait for timeout or exit7. No file reads/writes, network or descendants.
owned_child_policy.purpose: Meaningful bounded OS timeout/cancellation experiment, not campaign-duration filler
owned_child_policy.verification: Parse own child PID from captured stdout; immediately check absent via os.kill(pid,0). No external process is signaled.

criteria: Actual subprocess.run returns completed checked exit7 or raises TimeoutExpired with owned PID stdout.
Child PID absent after subprocess.run cleanup/error; no descendants created by owned code.
Cached failure leaves successful request/result/receipt bytes and budgets unchanged. Unchanged helper raises; isolated prior candidate REFUSED/no quote.
Fresh failure durably records INCONCLUSIVE; duplicate same ID returns original INCONCLUSIVE without launching child again.
Normal native parser recovery succeeds under cached ID or a fresh distinct request ID as appropriate; locks released.
limits: Replacement extraction function launches owned Python child, not a hung native Go parser or full real outage.
No cross-process lock, Windows, application source execution or general cancellation certification.
